figures.finding: American Samoa levies its own income tax, modeled on the US Internal Revenue Code as in effect on 31 December 2000 (A.S.C.A. § 11.0403); the Tax Office issues the 2000 tax table and rate schedules with its Form 390, so a single filer pays 15% to $26,250, 28% to $63,550, 31% to $132,600, 36% to $288,350 and 39.6% above.
figures.applies: Rates on taxable income after the 2000 Code's deductions and exemptions (their amounts not read here); territorial changes such as the child tax credit apply.

sources.said: American Samoa has its own separate and independent income tax system that is modeled on the U.S. income tax laws in the Internal Revenue Code as in effect on December 31, 2000.

The Samoan Income Tax Act consists of chapters 4 and 5 of the American Samoa Code and the provisions of the United States Internal Revenue Code adopted by § 11.0403(a).

figures.finding: US Social Security and Medicare taxes (FICA) apply to employment in American Samoa.
figures.applies: Rates and ceiling as in the United States.

sources.said: Employers and employees within American Samoa must pay U.S. Social Security taxes, as the Federal Insurance Contributions Act applies to any employment performed within the United States or to any employment performed outside the United States by her citizens or residents for an American employer.

figures.finding: The American Samoa Government collects income tax by withholding from wages, by periodic estimated payments and otherwise.

figures.finding: Returns for a year are filed in the following year's filing season, which for 2024 returns opened on 27 January 2025.
figures.applies: Calendar year as under the Code; the due date was not read.

sources.said: Tax filing season will commence on the 27th of January 2025

figures.finding: On top of the income tax, all wages earned in the Territory bear a 2% wage tax, paid by the wage earner with his return (since tax year 2012).

value.appliesTo: all wages earned in the Territory

sources.said: (a) All wages earned in the Territory shall be taxed at the rate of two percent (2%). This tax is in addition to American Samoa’s income tax as set forth in Chapters 4 and 5 of this Title. (b) This tax shall be paid by the wage earner and reported on the wage earner’s tax return. (c) Employers shall immediately increase the minimum withholding for all employees from 4% to 6%. (d) This wage tax shall take effect and commence in tax year 2012.

figures.finding: Employers must withhold at least 6% of every employee's wages (raised from 4% when the 2% wage tax began in 2012).

figures.finding: Withholding on non-resident aliens follows chapter 3 of the US Internal Revenue Code as American Samoa adopted it (as in effect on 31 December 2000), with local amendments to sections 1441 and 1442; wages a non-resident earns in the Territory also bear the 2% wage tax.

value.regime: IRC chapter 3 (sections 1441-1442) as adopted at 31 December 2000

figures.applies: The rate itself is the adopted IRC's (not quoted here).

The income tax and the income tax rules in force in the United States of America in effect on December 31, 2000, where not clearly inapplicable or incompatible with the intent of this section, are adopted by American Samoa, and shall be deemed to impose a separate Territorial income tax, payable to the government.

(a) All wages earned in the Territory shall be taxed at the rate of two percent (2%). This tax is in addition to American Samoa’s income tax as set forth in Chapters 4 and 5 of this Title. (b) This tax shall be paid by the wage earner and reported on the wage earner’s tax return. (c) Employers shall immediately increase the minimum withholding for all employees from 4% to 6%. (d) This wage tax shall take effect and commence in tax year 2012.

figures.finding: American Samoa has no VAT, GST or general sales tax: its revenue title (A.S.C.A. Title 11) provides an income tax, a wage tax, a machine and device tax, excise taxes on imports and exports and a secondhand imported items tax, so a freelancer's fee bears none.
figures.applies: A.S.C.A. Title 11 as the Bar Association publishes it (2026).
